angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 904,410 km at 105.98 pc = 0.11 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 9.4360 +/- 0.0208 mas (same row, RUWE 0.98): 105.98 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.3 +/- 0.009 solar radii from Lund et al. 2019, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HIP 41378 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..248L/abstract): 904,410 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.22 +/- 0.03 solar masses from Lund et al. 2019, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HIP 41378 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..248L/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6290 +/- 77 K from Lund et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HIP 41378 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..248L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Lund et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HIP 41378 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..248L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hip-41378.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.297, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
